title: Clean Data to Clear Decisions
subject: Build and test a fictional operations summary in the in-course data-workflow sandbox

objectiveEvidence.objective: Trace input, artifact and earlier-output references in an ordered sandbox workflow.
Remove outer whitespace while preserving meaningful internal text.
Normalize a comparison label with lowercase without changing the original input.
Create an uppercase display code from a cleaned value.
Compose a template from named inputs, artifact fields and prior outputs.
Choose the second reference when the first value is empty or whitespace only.
Calculate a total by summing finite numeric-string references.
Multiply an earlier numeric total by a supplied numeric factor.
Evaluate sample and changed-input runs against explicit project criteria before submission.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Read and copy values
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 1 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. A reference names one available value: input.name is supplied case data, values.name is an editable artifact field, and output.name is an earlier step result. Copy reads one reference without altering its text. Earlier outputs must be created before use; unknown or forward references stop the run. Case: input.ticket is T-104. Copy input.ticket into ticketId.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Trim outer spaces
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 2 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. Trim removes whitespace from the beginning and end, not the middle. Copy preserves outer spaces. Case: input.name is "  Ada Lee  ". Trim input.name into cleanName to obtain "Ada Lee"; the internal space remains. Do not use case conversion as a substitute for trimming.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Normalize text case
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 3 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. Lowercase converts letters to lower case but does not remove spaces. First trim a label, then lowercase the earlier trimmed output. Case: input.team is "  SuPPORT  ". Trim into teamTrim, then lowercase output.teamTrim into teamKey to produce "support". Input data stays unchanged.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Format a display code
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 4 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. Uppercase converts letters to upper case and preserves nonletters. Trim input.code into codeTrim before uppercase output.codeTrim into displayCode. Case: "  ab-7 " becomes "AB-7". A display code can differ from a lowercase comparison key. Case conversion alone does not validate a code.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Compose a readable summary
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 5 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. Template inserts references written in double braces and preserves surrounding literal text. Case format: {{values.prefix}} | {{output.ticketId}} | {{output.cleanName}} | {{output.teamKey}} | {{output.displayCode}} | {{output.contact}}. The prefix is the artifact field "Review". A template formats data; it does not send messages or approve work. Build referenced outputs first.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Choose a fallback safely
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 6 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. Fallback takes two references separated by |. It keeps a nonblank first value; otherwise it uses the second. Trim input.contact into contactTrim, then fallback output.contactTrim | values.defaultContact into contact. Default artifact value is "Unassigned". Case: a blank contact uses Unassigned, while " Ada " becomes Ada and is kept. Fallback is a formatting convention, not permission to invent missing real facts.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Add numeric inputs
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 7 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. Sum adds comma-separated references; literal numeric constants are not references. Every value must be a nonblank finite numeric string; blank or nonnumeric values stop the run. Sum input.base, input.extra into totalUnits. In a fictional kit case, base 8 and extra 2 produce 10. This is an exercise count, not a financial calculation.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Multiply a calculated total
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 8 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. Multiply uses comma-separated numeric references and requires nonblank finite numbers. Multiply output.totalUnits, input.factor into plannedUnits, after totalUnits is created. For totalUnits 10 and factor 3 the result is 30. This computes a fictional planning quantity and neither reserves nor delivers real kits.

sources.title: Fictional sandbox reference: Test before submitting
sources.reference: FICTIONAL TRAINING SOURCE 9 — authored for this course from the local data-workflow runtime contract, not an independently supplied company policy. Run simulates the sample and shows outputs and step trace. Test project checks every declared case without recording a submission. Save draft persists editable work; Submit project recomputes the grade and records a submission. Check both changed inputs and missing-value behavior rather than hard-coding sample outputs. If all criteria are required, every criterion must pass. An interpreter error prevents passing. Test success does not establish a real external action.

miniProject.title: Build a tested operations review card
miniProject.brief: Combine all nine topics in one ordered sandbox workflow. Clean synthetic text, choose a safe blank-contact label, compose a review summary, calculate a fictional planning quantity and verify both cases. This is a bounded simulation, with no external actions.
miniProject.deliverable: One saved and submitted sandbox artifact containing the four completed fields, ordered transformation steps and eight required named outputs, passing all nine criteria across both supplied cases.
rubric: Copy the current ticket without alteration.
Trim outer name padding and retain the internal space.
Normalize the current team key after trimming.
Create a clean uppercase display code.
Compose the exact review format from current outputs.
Handle both blank and present contacts.
Add the supplied counts for both cases.
Multiply the computed total by the supplied factor.
Validate both cases and document the evidence boundary.

instructions: 1. Inspect the two synthetic test cases and grading criteria. Build one review-card workflow; all work stays inside this course. No message is sent and no real kit is reserved.

2. Fill prefix with Review and defaultContact with Unassigned. In testPlan explain why you check both blank and present contact cases. Set status to Simulation only; no real action. These are editable artifact fields, referenced through values.name.
3. Create ticketId with copy from input.ticket. Trim input.name into cleanName. Trim input.team into teamTrim, then lowercase output.teamTrim into teamKey. Keep the output names exactly as stated.
4. Trim input.code into codeTrim, then uppercase output.codeTrim into displayCode. Trim input.contact into contactTrim. Use fallback with output.contactTrim | values.defaultContact to create contact.

5. After those outputs exist, create summary with template. Format exactly: {{values.prefix}} | {{output.ticketId}} | {{output.cleanName}} | {{output.teamKey}} | {{output.displayCode}} | {{output.contact}}. Literal spaces and separators are part of the required format.
6. Use sum with input.base, input.extra to create totalUnits. Use multiply with output.totalUnits, input.factor to create plannedUnits. Numeric expressions use references, not literal sample values.

7. Run to inspect sample outputs and step trace. Test project checks both cases, including changed strings, a present contact and different counts. A fixed sample output fails the changed case; blank or nonnumeric count data causes an error rather than silently becoming zero.

8. Save draft, inspect any failed criteria, revise and retest. Submit project records the artifact and server-computed grade. Every one of the nine criteria must pass. Only a passing submission enables the final assessment. Allow about twelve minutes; no external tools are required.
